A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GFlowNet-based red-teaming study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original red-teaming, attack-transfer, safety-tuning, and ablation experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including comparisons across target models and downstream evaluations after safety tuning.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3 retain the same GFlowNet training, prompt filtering, and MLE smoothing procedure. Reranking-based adaptation to other target models is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SafetyDataset/AdvBench training data, five primary target models, transfer targets including GPT-4o, Gemma safety-tuning task, and six downstream benchmarks in Table B.2.

E2.justification: SFT, ICL, REINFORCE, PPO + Novelty, and GFlowNet remain the same comparison methods in the corresponding experiments. Comparator membership also matches in the ablations.

E3.justification: Both retain the same toxicity and cosine-distance metrics, 10,000-prompt main evaluations, and 1,024-prompt transfer and safety-tuning experiments. Model configurations, evaluation procedures, and Appendix A training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The attacker-size comparison, reranking analysis, temperature sensitivity study, and dataset-collection ablation are retained unchanged. Appendix B also preserves the classifier ablation, downstream evaluation, and example attacks and responses.

E5.justification: Five-run reporting and standard deviations in Tables B.3–B.4 are unchanged, as are uncertainty displays elsewhere. Neither version adds or revises seed information or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries, plot data, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 3 retains GFlowNet + MLE's 85.16% source toxicity rate on Gemma-2b-it and 27.39% transfer toxicity rate on Llama-2-7b-chat.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same mathematical definitions and Equations 1–4, including the reward, trajectory-balance objective, and sampled log-reward approximation. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about diverse effective attacks, transferability, inexpensive adaptation, and robust safety tuning without degrading downstream performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the diversity–toxicity trade-off, transferability, and reward hacking are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning classifier dependence, contextual definitions of harm, and the cost of querying target models.

D1.justification: Appendix A preserves the same optimizer settings, training budgets, filtering thresholds, and hardware information. Table 4's resource measurements and the code-access information also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to red-teaming, jailbreak, and GFlowNet research.

P1.justification: The front-page author listing and arXiv version/date information are updated. The scientific prose, section sequence, and appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are small typesetting differences in spacing and caption wrapping, notably Table 1. Figures and tables retain their scientific content, structure, numbering, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves v2's method, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The author/version updates and minor typesetting changes produce no meaningful net difference in the paper's overall quality.
